content:
Elaine (support): Heads-up — a customer escalated a rerank request that works in their dev console but fails from our Console cURL snippet. They see mixed errors: 400/422 and sometimes 'unexpected_score' or 'scores: NaN'.

Diego (engineer): ugh. Do we have the exact cURL they ran and the error body? Could be quoting/escaping or array vs object mismatch.

Elaine (support): Pasting what the customer copied from our Console 'Copy cURL' (they're on macOS):

```bash
# from Console button copy
curl https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/rerank \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  --data '{\n    "query": "best pizza toppings",\n    "candidates": [\n      { "text": "pepperoni" },\n      { "text": "mushrooms" },\n    ],\n    "return_scores": true,\n  }'\n```

Elaine (support): Customer gets: 400 Bad Request with body:

```json
{ "error": "invalid_json", "message": "Trailing comma at position 123" }
```

Diego (engineer): That payload clearly has trailing commas — our Console snippet shows a pretty-printed JSON block and users often copy paste it into single-quoted --data which on some shells removes line breaks or preserves trailing whitespace. Also some shells (zsh) will add bash-style quote behavior.

Diego (engineer): Repro steps I ran locally (worked to reproduce):
1) Copy the Console snippet into Terminal on macOS Big Sur (zsh) -> causes trailing commas to stay.
2) Run the curl -> 400 invalid_json (trailing comma).

Diego (engineer): But the other errors (NaN / unexpected_score) came from them sending candidates as a single string of JSON (escaped) because they pasted into an Azure Cloud Shell which wrapped things differently. Example bad payload they tried:

```bash
# Azure Cloud Shell (bad):
curl https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data "{\"query\":\"best pizza toppings\",\"candidates\":\"[{\\\"text\\\":\\\"pepperoni\\\"}]\",\"return_scores\":true}"
```

Diego (engineer): In that case server sees candidates as a string, then our server attempts to parse candidate scores after reranking and ends up with NaN -> we return 422 with body: `{"error":"invalid_candidate_format","message":"candidates must be array of objects"}`.

Elaine (support): Customer also reported a docs inconsistency: our Console shows the top-level field as `candidates` array of strings in one place, and the CLI example shows `candidates` as array of objects with `text` — that confused them. Nina, tagging docs to confirm. @Nina

Nina (docs): Thanks @Elaine — I can see two spots where examples diverge (quickstart vs advanced). I’ll patch both. Quick fix: update quickstart to show object form ("text") and add a note that shell quoting matters.

Nina (docs): Proposed snippet for Console/CLI (safe portable):

```bash
# POSIX shell (macOS / Linux) - compact single-line, safe for copy/paste
curl https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  --data-binary $'{"query":"best pizza toppings","candidates":[{"text":"pepperoni"},{"text":"mushrooms"}],"return_scores":true}'
```

Nina (docs): And Windows CMD note:
```cmd
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/rerank -H "Authorization: Bearer %REDWOOD_KEY%" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"query\":\"best pizza toppings\",\"candidates\":[{\"text\":\"pepperoni\"}],\"return_scores\":true}"
```

Matt (sre): Also add a server-side guard to return a clearer error when candidates is a string vs array. Right now it bubbles into the score pipeline and becomes `scores: NaN`. We should detect types early and return 400 with `invalid_field_type`. I'll open a small PR.

support-bot: Incident / Escalation Log - created incident INC-2024-742: "rerank endpoint - docs/console formatting causing malformed requests" (priority: P2)

Diego (engineer): For support triage — recommended troubleshooting checklist to share with customers: 
- Ask for raw cURL they ran (exact paste).
- Ask which shell / OS they used (zsh, bash, powershell, azure cloud shell).
- Request full response body (include headers).
- Try `--data-binary` or compact single-line JSON (see docs snippet).
- If they use a client SDK, ask for the dict/JSON object they're sending (not a stringified JSON inside another string).

Elaine (support): I sent that checklist + suggested fixes. Customer replied they'll try `--data-binary` and update.

Nina (docs): I'll push the examples and add a short "Common cURL quoting pitfalls" section with examples for the three major shells.

Matt (sre): PR opened to validate candidate array shape and return 400 with message: `{"error":"invalid_field_type","field":"candidates","expected":"array"}`. Will include unit tests (node + python).

Elaine (support): Thanks everyone. I'll wait for the customer's confirmation and close INC-2024-742 once they verify. Leaving thread open for the follow-up logs.

Diego (engineer): FYI — also saw minor mismatch in console: the copy button was including a trailing comma when pretty printing. Nina, if you want I can strip trailing commas in the copy flow (safe).

Nina (docs): If we fix Console copy behavior that's best. I'll still keep the docs defensive with examples and notes.

Elaine (support): Resolved for now: customer confirmed `--data-binary` fixed the 400, and the server PR fixed the 422 path locally. Will update once they finish end-to-end tests.
